This module provides functionality to render tokens as line-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each token is emitted as a self-contained JSON object on its own line, making the output easy to stream over websocket/udp for syntax highlighting in editors and other higher-level applications.

Every token object exposes:

  • kind: the raw token kind (e.g. "ident", "string", "comment")
  • scope: a TextMate-style scope derived from the token kind and attributes
  • attr: user-defined attributes (e.g. keyword names, YAML filter hits)
  • line, col: 1-based line/column of the token start
  • start, stop: byte offsets into the source (stop is exclusive)
  • value: the token lexeme (source text)

proc scopeForToken(lexer: SweetLexer; tok: Token): string {....raises: [KeyError],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}

Derive a TextMate-style scope for the given token, based on the token kind and the tables declared in the syntax YAML spec.

Keyword classification is entirely the spec's business: a spec lists the lexemes it wants scoped in keyword_scopes and the renderer just looks the lexeme up, so no vocabulary is baked in here. A spec that declares no scopes gets a flat keyword for every identifier it lists. tok.attr holds keyword lexemes (e.g. "int", "if"), not semantic classes, so it is never used to classify. YAML filters (CSS, Markdown) are the exception: their dotted attrs (e.g. "markup.heading") map 1:1 to scopes.
